decision.question: Are both giraffes and the substantial surrounding scene represented through drawn contours, interior marks and shading rather than retained photographic rendering?
decision.criteria: Pass if drawn contours, interior marks and constructed shading represent both giraffes and substantial surrounding regions. Evaluate the giraffes' bodies, spots and legs separately from the vegetation, hills, sky and ground; neither region alone establishes satisfaction. Broad directional strokes and blended drawn shading may represent simplified environmental forms without preserving fine detail. Fail if substantial areas in either region still depend on retained photographic surface detail or photographic modeling, with only added outlines, grain or blur. Distinguish photographic modeling through retained source-specific detail and tonal structure not re-expressed by drawn marks; accurate anatomy, detailed spots, smooth gradients, dark shading and source resemblance are not by themselves proof of photographic rendering. Texture and smudging alone establish neither drawing nor photography. Return unknown only when evidence is unavailable or genuinely insufficient to distinguish the rendering, not simply because different regions provide different evidence.
